answer: Each identity claims one umber channel in the nebula signal band, posts a 70-credit bond, and files a signed log of its serial and signal samples. An auditor recomputes each log against the band plan; a channel claimed twice, a serial on two logs, or samples mismatching the spectrum burns the bond. First 30 credits, kth 30+6(k-1), 1000th 6024; 1000 fakes pay 3,027,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-transmitter ring fails: one serial cannot back two signal logs, so the scan voids both and burns both bonds. An honest operator files once, pays 30, and recovers the 70 bond after audit.
